of replicate cohorts, so a rule can be scored against the truth and by
the statistics a split of a real cohort gives.
:::

# Scores on the fourth bank

::: {.reuse}
The first block of `lfcse-bank-4` (`r num_first4` examples,
`r 4 * num_first4` fitted cohorts). `raw` is run with the same libraries
as `donor_wls`; no covariate varies within a donor, so there is no `_cov`
variant and `@total` is the summed-count library with the donor-level
design.
:::

```{r bank4_scores}
level_df <- data.frame(
  factor = c("rank", "rank", "shape", "shape"),
  level = c("5", "30", "gabitto_like", "green_like"),
  label = c("Rank 5", "Rank 30", "Gabitto-like", "Green-like"),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
score4_df <- wide4(focus_vec, level_df)
score4_df <- score4_df[order(score4_df[["Gabitto-like"]]), ]
knitr::kable(score4_df, row.names = FALSE,
             caption = "Table 18. Mean score against the truth (nats per gene, lower is better) on the first block of the fourth bank, ordered by the Gabitto-like cohorts: 40 or 80 donors, a third of them controls, fitted at rank 30. Green-like: 200 donors, a third of them controls, rank 30.")
```

```{r bank4_diagnostics}
diag4_df <- data.frame(
  Method = paste0("`", focus_vec, "`"),
  RMSE = sapply(focus_vec, b4, col = "rmse", factor = "rank", level = "30"),
  `Coverage of 95%` = sapply(focus_vec, b4, col = "coverage_95",
                             factor = "rank", level = "30"),
  slope_weak = sapply(focus_vec, b4, col = "slope_weak", factor = "rank",
                      level = "30"),
  slope_deg = sapply(focus_vec, b4, col = "slope_deg", factor = "rank",
                     level = "30"),
  se_strong = sapply(focus_vec, b4, col = "se_strong", factor = "rank",
                     level = "30"),
  `vs DESeq2 (SE)` = sapply(focus_vec, function(method){
    paste0(fmt(b4(method, col = "vs_deseq2", factor = "rank", level = "30")),
           " (", fmt(b4(method, col = "vs_deseq2_se", factor = "rank",
                        level = "30")), ")")
  }),
  `Wins over DESeq2` = sapply(focus_vec, function(method){
    pct(b4(method, col = "win_deseq2", factor = "rank", level = "30"))
  }),
  check.names = FALSE
)
knitr::kable(diag4_df, row.names = FALSE, digits = 3,
             caption = "Table 19. Diagnostics at rank 30 on the first block. `slope_deg` is the slope of the logFC on the truth over the true DEGs (true log2 fold change of 0.25 or more), the gate on retained signal of section 16.")
```

```{r fig_bank4_rank, fig.width=9, fig.height=5, fig.cap="Figure 6. Mean score against the truth on the first block of the fourth bank at the two fitted ranks, with one standard error. The dashed line is DESeq2, which does not read the fit."}
plot_df <- strata4_df[strata4_df$factor == "rank" &
                        strata4_df$method %in% focus_vec, ]
order_vec <- plot_df$method[plot_df$level == "30"]
order_vec <- order_vec[order(-plot_df$score[plot_df$level == "30"])]
plot_df$method <- factor(plot_df$method, levels = order_vec)
plot_df$rank <- paste0("rank ", plot_df$level)
plot1 <- ggplot2::ggplot(plot_df, ggplot2::aes(x = score, y = method,
                                               color = rank))
plot1 <- plot1 + ggplot2::geom_vline(xintercept = b4("deseq2"),
                                     linetype = "dashed", color = "grey50")
plot1 <- plot1 + ggplot2::geom_errorbarh(ggplot2::aes(xmin = score - score_se,
                                                      xmax = score + score_se),
                                         height = 0.2)
plot1 <- plot1 + ggplot2::geom_point(size = 2.5)
plot1 <- plot1 + ggplot2::scale_color_manual(values = c("rank 5" = "#1f77b4",
                                                        "rank 30" = "#ff7f0e"),
                                             name = "Fitted rank")
plot1 <- plot1 + ggplot2::labs(x = "Score (nats per gene, lower is better)",
                               y = NULL)
plot1 <- plot1 + ggplot2::theme_bw()
plot(plot1)
```

```{r bank4_pieces}
p_wls_deseq2 <- paired4("donor_wls@esvd_nofloor", "deseq2")
p_wls_raw <- paired4("donor_wls@esvd_nofloor", "raw@esvd_nofloor")
p_wls_raw5 <- paired4("donor_wls@esvd_nofloor", "raw@esvd_nofloor",
                      df = first4_df[first4_df$rank == 5, ])
p_wls_raw30 <- paired4("donor_wls@esvd_nofloor", "raw@esvd_nofloor",
                       df = first4_df[first4_df$rank == 30, ])
p_wls_rawfloor <- paired4("donor_wls", "raw")
p_floor_wls <- paired4("donor_wls@esvd_nofloor", "donor_wls")
p_total_wls <- paired4("donor_wls@esvd_nofloor", "donor_wls@total")
gb4 <- function(method, bin, rank, col = "rmse", bin_type = "depth"){
  bool_vec <- bins4_df$method == method & bins4_df$bin == bin &
    bins4_df$rank == rank & bins4_df$bin_type == bin_type
  stopifnot(sum(bool_vec) == 1)
  bins4_df[[col]][bool_vec]
}
```

**The donor-level regression and pseudobulk DESeq2 are level on this
bank, and both are ahead of every other rule that passes the gates.**
`state_adjusted` heads the Gabitto-like column of Table 18 and fails both
slope gates at rank 30 (below), so it is set aside here. Over the first
block
`donor_wls@esvd_nofloor` scores `r fmt(b4("donor_wls@esvd_nofloor"))` and
`deseq2` `r fmt(b4("deseq2"))`, a paired difference of
`r fmt(p_wls_deseq2$diff)` (SE `r fmt(p_wls_deseq2$se)`), where
`donor_wls` led by 0.05 to 0.25 nats on banks 1 to 3. The bank has no
confounder within donors, no depth error and twice to twenty times the
cells of the earlier banks' cohorts, the setting in which section 6 found
a donor-level analysis sufficient. The library changes `donor_wls` little
here: the floor costs it `r fmt(-p_floor_wls$diff)` nats and the summed
counts are within `r fmt(abs(p_total_wls$diff))` of the unfloored fitted
library.

**`raw` is behind `donor_wls` with every library.** With the floored
fitted library, the form the loops ran, `raw` trails `donor_wls` by
`r fmt(-p_wls_rawfloor$diff)` nats (SE `r fmt(p_wls_rawfloor$se)`), and
its 95% interval covers the truth
`r pct(b4("raw", col = "coverage_95"), 1)` of the time against
`r pct(b4("donor_wls", col = "coverage_95"), 1)`: an unmoderated variance
of 13 to 100 donors per arm with a normal reference is too small. With
the summed counts `raw` has no adjustment for the donor-level covariates
at all, since it has no design and the library is its only adjustment,
and it scores `r fmt(b4("raw@total"))`. With the unfloored fitted library
it trails by `r fmt(-p_wls_raw5$diff)` at rank 5 and by
`r fmt(-p_wls_raw30$diff)` at rank 30, where its RMSE is
`r fmt(b4("raw@esvd_nofloor", col = "rmse", factor = "rank", level = "30"), 2)`
against
`r fmt(b4("donor_wls@esvd_nofloor", col = "rmse", factor = "rank", level = "30"), 2)`.
The loss at rank 30 comes from the genes whose fitted depth coefficient
is far from 1 (section 11): `raw` averages each cell's count over its
library, so a cell with a library of $10^{-4}$ and one count dominates a
donor's mean, while `donor_wls` divides the donor's summed count by its
summed library. Over the affected genes the RMSE of `raw@esvd_nofloor`
at rank 30 is
`r fmt(gb4("raw@esvd_nofloor", "depth_beyond", 30), 2)` against
`r fmt(gb4("donor_wls@esvd_nofloor", "depth_beyond", 30), 2)`, and over
the other genes
`r fmt(gb4("raw@esvd_nofloor", "depth_within", 30), 2)` against
`r fmt(gb4("donor_wls@esvd_nofloor", "depth_within", 30), 2)`, so the
instability is not confined to the genes beyond the threshold of 1.

**The gates.** `gap_trend` fails `se_strong` for the fourth time
(`r fmt(b4("gap_trend", col = "se_strong", factor = "rank", level = "30"), 2)`).
At rank 30 `state_adjusted` has a `slope_weak` of
`r fmt(b4("state_adjusted", col = "slope_weak", factor = "rank", level = "30"), 2)`
and a `slope_deg` of
`r fmt(b4("state_adjusted", col = "slope_deg", factor = "rank", level = "30"), 2)`,
where neither truth includes a state difference between the arms: it
reports about a fifth of every effect. Its RMSE at rank 30
(`r fmt(b4("state_adjusted", col = "rmse", factor = "rank", level = "30"), 2)`)
is the lowest of Table 19 because most true effects of this bank are
small against their sampling error, and a rule that shrinks every logFC
towards zero is then closer to the truth on average, which is the reason
the loops gated the slope. Section 13 takes the rank up. Every other
rule has both slopes within 0.05 of 1.
`stored` covers the truth
`r pct(b4("stored", col = "coverage_95", factor = "rank", level = "30"), 1)`
of the time, an SE far too large, and `null_rescaled`
`r pct(b4("null_rescaled", col = "coverage_95", factor = "rank", level = "30"), 1)`.

::: {.takeaway}
On cohorts shaped like the two real ones, with donor-level covariates
only, `donor_wls` and pseudobulk DESeq2 are equally accurate and the
rest of the order is that of banks 1 to 3. `raw` is behind `donor_wls`
whichever library it is handed: its SE is too small with few donors, it
has no design for the covariates, and on the unfloored library it is
unstable for the genes whose fitted depth coefficient is far from 1.
:::

# Rank near the donor count

::: {.reuse}
The first block of `lfcse-bank-4`: every cohort at rank 5 and at rank 30,
by the number of donors.
:::

```{r bank4_rank_table}
rank_method_vec <- c("stored", "raw@esvd_nofloor", "donor_wls@esvd_nofloor",
                     "embed_prior@esvd_nofloor", "state_adjusted",
                     "state_adjusted@esvd_nofloor", "deseq2")
rank_level_df <- data.frame(
  factor = "rank_donors",
  level = c("k5_n40", "k30_n40", "k5_n80", "k30_n80", "k5_n200", "k30_n200"),
  label = c("rank 5, 40 donors", "rank 30, 40 donors", "rank 5, 80 donors",
            "rank 30, 80 donors", "rank 5, 200 donors", "rank 30, 200 donors"),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
knitr::kable(wide4(rank_method_vec, rank_level_df, col = "slope_deg",
                   digits = 2),
             row.names = FALSE,
             caption = "Table 20. `slope_deg`, the slope of the reported logFC on the truth over the true DEGs, by fitted rank and number of donors (first block). 1 means the true effects are reported at full size.")
knitr::kable(wide4(rank_method_vec, rank_level_df, digits = 3),
             row.names = FALSE,
             caption = "Table 21. The score against the truth in the same strata.")
```

**At rank 30 `state_adjusted` reports a fifth to a quarter of the true
effect, whatever the number of donors.** Its `slope_deg` is
`r fmt(b4("state_adjusted", col = "slope_deg", factor = "rank_donors", level = "k30_n40"), 2)`,
`r fmt(b4("state_adjusted", col = "slope_deg", factor = "rank_donors", level = "k30_n80"), 2)`
and
`r fmt(b4("state_adjusted", col = "slope_deg", factor = "rank_donors", level = "k30_n200"), 2)`
at 40, 80 and 200 donors, against
`r fmt(b4("state_adjusted", col = "slope_deg", factor = "rank", level = "5"), 2)`
at rank 5 on the same cohorts (Table 20). The rule subtracts from each
gene's arm coefficient its component along the fitted loadings, and with
30 loadings over 600 genes that component is most of the coefficient,
whether the cohort has 40 donors or 200. The Gabitto report had named
the rank relative to the donor count; the Green halves (214 donors) and
the 200-donor cohorts of this bank show that the rank alone is enough.
The score against the truth sees the failure only where the effects are
well measured: at rank 30 `state_adjusted` scores
`r fmt(b4("state_adjusted", factor = "rank_donors", level = "k30_n200"))`
against
`r fmt(b4("donor_wls@esvd_nofloor", factor = "rank_donors", level = "k30_n200"))`
for `donor_wls@esvd_nofloor` at 200 donors and
`r fmt(b4("state_adjusted", factor = "rank_donors", level = "k30_n40"))`
against
`r fmt(b4("donor_wls@esvd_nofloor", factor = "rank_donors", level = "k30_n40"))`
at 40 (Table 21), where shrinking every effect by four fifths costs less
than the noise it removes. The slope gates see it at every donor count.

**At rank 5 `state_adjusted` is the best rule of this bank and passes
the gates.** It scores
`r fmt(b4("state_adjusted", factor = "rank", level = "5"))` against
`r fmt(b4("donor_wls@esvd_nofloor", factor = "rank", level = "5"))` for
`donor_wls@esvd_nofloor`, with a `slope_weak` of
`r fmt(b4("state_adjusted", col = "slope_weak", factor = "rank", level = "5"), 2)`,
because half of the examples have donor-level cell states that a rank-5
embedding recovers and the rule removes from the donor variance. This is
what the second loop found on its own bank, also fitted at rank 5.

**No other rule depends on the rank, except through the library.**
`donor_wls@esvd_nofloor` scores
`r fmt(b4("donor_wls@esvd_nofloor", factor = "rank", level = "5"))` at
rank 5 and
`r fmt(b4("donor_wls@esvd_nofloor", factor = "rank", level = "30"))` at
rank 30, and `embed_prior`, which reads the embedding for its variance
prior, is within 0.01 of it at both. `stored` moves by
`r fmt(abs(b4("stored", factor = "rank", level = "5") - b4("stored", factor = "rank", level = "30")))`.
`raw@esvd_nofloor` is the exception of section 12.

::: {.takeaway}
A bank factor for the fitted rank exposes `state_adjusted`: at the
default rank of 30 it removes about four fifths of every true effect at
40, 80 and 200 donors, which is what its two real-cohort failures look
like. At rank 5 the same rule is valid and the most accurate of the
bank, so its use depends on a second fit at a low rank, which no real
cohort has yet been given. The donor-level rules do not read the
embedding and do not move with the rank.
:::

# Few controls, unbalanced arms and the number of donors

::: {.reuse}
The first block of `lfcse-bank-4` at rank 30, by `balance` and `donors`.
:::

```{r bank4_balance}
balance_method_vec <- c("stored", "null_rescaled", "raw", "raw@esvd_nofloor",
                        "donor_wls@esvd_nofloor", "deseq2")
balance_df <- first4_df[first4_df$rank == 30 &
                          first4_df$method %in% balance_method_vec, ]
balance_agg_df <- stats::aggregate(cbind(score, coverage_95) ~ method +
                                     balance + donors, data = balance_df,
                                   FUN = mean)
balance_table <- function(col, digits){
  out_df <- data.frame(Method = paste0("`", balance_method_vec, "`"),
                       stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  for(donors in c(40, 80, 200)){
    for(balance in c("half", "third")){
      out_df[[paste0(donors, " donors, ", balance)]] <-
        sapply(balance_method_vec, function(method){
          round(balance_agg_df[[col]][balance_agg_df$method == method &
                                        balance_agg_df$balance == balance &
                                        balance_agg_df$donors == donors],
                digits)
        })
    }
  }
  out_df
}
bal <- function(method, col, balance, donors){
  balance_agg_df[[col]][balance_agg_df$method == method &
                          balance_agg_df$balance == balance &
                          balance_agg_df$donors == donors]
}
knitr::kable(balance_table("coverage_95", 3), row.names = FALSE,
             caption = "Table 22. Coverage of the 95% interval at rank 30 by number of donors and share of controls (`half`, or a `third`).")
knitr::kable(balance_table("score", 3), row.names = FALSE,
             caption = "Table 23. The score against the truth in the same strata.")
```

**The interval of `donor_wls` keeps its coverage with 13 controls, and
the interval of `raw` does not.** At 40 donors with a third of them
controls `donor_wls@esvd_nofloor` covers the truth
`r pct(bal("donor_wls@esvd_nofloor", "coverage_95", "third", 40), 1)` of
the time and DESeq2
`r pct(bal("deseq2", "coverage_95", "third", 40), 1)`, against
`r pct(bal("raw", "coverage_95", "third", 40), 1)` for `raw` and
`r pct(bal("raw@esvd_nofloor", "coverage_95", "third", 40), 1)` for
`raw@esvd_nofloor` (Table 22). `raw` estimates each arm's variance from
that arm's donors alone, 13 of them here, and refers the statistic to a
normal; `donor_wls` pools the residual variance over both arms and
moderates it across genes. At 200 donors the coverage of `raw` is
`r pct(bal("raw", "coverage_95", "third", 200), 1)`.

**Unbalanced arms cost `donor_wls` and DESeq2 the same precision.** From
half to a third of the donors as controls the score of
`donor_wls@esvd_nofloor` moves from
`r fmt(bal("donor_wls@esvd_nofloor", "score", "half", 40))` to
`r fmt(bal("donor_wls@esvd_nofloor", "score", "third", 40))` at 40 donors
and DESeq2's from `r fmt(bal("deseq2", "score", "half", 40))` to
`r fmt(bal("deseq2", "score", "third", 40))`, the loss of a contrast whose
smaller arm has 13 donors in place of 20. The two stay within 0.02 nats
of each other in all six columns of Table 23, ahead of the other four
rules in each.

::: {.takeaway}
The split-half reports asked whether few controls break the moderation
or the degrees of freedom of `donor_wls`. They do not: its coverage is
within a point of nominal at 13 controls against 27 cases. The rule that
few controls hurt is `raw`, whose interval is too short by a margin that
shrinks as donors are added.
:::

# The calls of each rule's test

::: {.reuse}
The first block of `lfcse-bank-4` at rank 30. Each rule's own test is the
Wald test of its pair, $z = \widehat\beta_g / s_g$ against the standard
normal with BH at 5% over the cohort's genes, as in the split-half
reports; DESeq2's is its adjusted p-value; the package's test is the
posterior-based one of 1.2.0. A false discovery is a called gene whose
true effect is exactly zero (`deg = half_null` only). A sign error is a
called gene with a nonzero effect whose reported logFC has the wrong
sign. A true DEG has a true log2 fold change of 0.25 or more.
:::

```{r bank4_calls}
call_method_vec <- c("null_rescaled", "raw", "raw@esvd_nofloor", "raw_null",
                     "donor_wls", "donor_wls@esvd_nofloor", "gap_trend",
                     "state_adjusted", "deseq2")
call_row <- function(label, method, test, factor = "rank", level = "30",
                     status = "all"){
  data.frame(
    Test = label,
    `Calls per cohort` = c4(method, "calls_per_cohort", test = test,
                            status = status, factor = factor, level = level),
    `False discovery proportion` = pct(c4(method, "fdp", test = test,
                                          status = status, factor = factor,
                                          level = level), 1),
    `Sign errors` = pct(c4(method, "sign_error", test = test, status = status,
                           factor = factor, level = level), 1),
    `Null or wrong sign` = pct(c4(method, "wrong", test = test,
                                  status = status, factor = factor,
                                  level = level), 1),
    `True DEGs called` = pct(c4(method, "power_deg", test = test,
                                status = status, factor = factor,
                                level = level)),
    check.names = FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
}
calls_out_df <- rbind(
  call_row("the package's test", "stored", "esvd"),
  do.call(rbind, lapply(call_method_vec, function(method){
    call_row(paste0("`", method, "`"), method, "own")
  }))
)
knitr::kable(calls_out_df, row.names = FALSE, digits = 1,
             caption = "Table 24. Calls at 5% FDR at rank 30 on the first block. The false discovery proportion is over the cohorts with exact nulls; the sign errors are a share of the calls with a nonzero truth, and their logFC is the `stored` one for the package's test.")
```

```{r bank4_calls_status}
status_out_df <- do.call(rbind, lapply(c("estimated", "capped"),
                                       function(status){
  rbind(
    cbind(Status = status, call_row("the package's test", "stored", "esvd",
                                    status = status)),
    cbind(Status = status,
          call_row("`donor_wls@esvd_nofloor`", "donor_wls@esvd_nofloor",
                   "own", status = status)),
    cbind(Status = status,
          call_row("`raw@esvd_nofloor`", "raw@esvd_nofloor", "own",
                   status = status))
  )
}))
knitr::kable(status_out_df, row.names = FALSE, digits = 1,
             caption = "Table 25. The same by the gene's nuisance status at rank 30: rate estimated, or at the cap or the boundary.")
```

```{r bank4_calls_shape}
shape_out_df <- do.call(rbind, lapply(c("gabitto_like", "green_like"),
                                      function(shape){
  label <- c(gabitto_like = "Gabitto-like", green_like = "Green-like")[[shape]]
  rbind(
    cbind(Cohorts = label, call_row("the package's test", "stored", "esvd",
                                    factor = "shape", level = shape)),
    cbind(Cohorts = label,
          call_row("`donor_wls@esvd_nofloor`", "donor_wls@esvd_nofloor",
                   "own", factor = "shape", level = shape)),
    cbind(Cohorts = label,
          call_row("`raw@esvd_nofloor`", "raw@esvd_nofloor", "own",
                   factor = "shape", level = shape)),
    cbind(Cohorts = label, call_row("`deseq2`", "deseq2", "own",
                                    factor = "shape", level = shape))
  )
}))
knitr::kable(shape_out_df, row.names = FALSE, digits = 1,
             caption = "Table 26. The same for the Gabitto-like cohorts (40 or 80 donors, a third of them controls) and the Green-like ones (200 donors, a third of them controls), at rank 30.")
```

**The Wald test of `donor_wls` holds its false discovery proportion and
the package's test does not.** At a nominal 5% the package's test has a
false discovery proportion of
`r pct(c4("stored", "fdp", test = "esvd", factor = "rank", level = "30"), 1)`
on this bank (18% and 19% on banks 2 and 3), the Wald test of
`donor_wls@esvd_nofloor`
`r pct(c4("donor_wls@esvd_nofloor", "fdp", factor = "rank", level = "30"), 1)`
and DESeq2
`r pct(c4("deseq2", "fdp", factor = "rank", level = "30"), 1)`
(Table 24). `donor_wls@esvd_nofloor` calls
`r pct(c4("donor_wls@esvd_nofloor", "power_deg", factor = "rank", level = "30"))`
of the true DEGs and the package's test
`r pct(c4("stored", "power_deg", test = "esvd", factor = "rank", level = "30"))`,
so the calibrated test gives up no power here. On the Gabitto-like
cohorts the Wald test of `donor_wls@esvd_nofloor` has
`r pct(c4("donor_wls@esvd_nofloor", "fdp", factor = "shape", level = "gabitto_like"), 1)`
and calls
`r pct(c4("donor_wls@esvd_nofloor", "power_deg", factor = "shape", level = "gabitto_like"))`
of the true DEGs, DESeq2
`r pct(c4("deseq2", "fdp", factor = "shape", level = "gabitto_like"), 1)`
and `r pct(c4("deseq2", "power_deg", factor = "shape", level = "gabitto_like"))`,
and the package's test
`r pct(c4("stored", "fdp", test = "esvd", factor = "shape", level = "gabitto_like"), 1)`
and
`r pct(c4("stored", "power_deg", test = "esvd", factor = "shape", level = "gabitto_like"))`
(Table 26). The Wald test of `raw@esvd_nofloor` has a false discovery
proportion of
`r pct(c4("raw@esvd_nofloor", "fdp", factor = "rank", level = "30"), 1)`
and that of `raw`
`r pct(c4("raw", "fdp", factor = "rank", level = "30"), 1)`, the
consequence of the short interval of section 14.

**Sign errors are under 5% for every test; false discoveries are what
differs.** Of the calls with a nonzero truth, the reported sign is wrong
for
`r pct(c4("stored", "sign_error", test = "esvd", factor = "rank", level = "30"), 1)`
of the package's calls and
`r pct(c4("donor_wls@esvd_nofloor", "sign_error", factor = "rank", level = "30"), 1)`
of `donor_wls@esvd_nofloor`'s. The split-half reports could only bound
the null share of the package's calls from the sign agreement between
the halves (at most 38% and 69% on Gabitto, 43% and 23% on Green); with a
truth, the share of its calls that are null or of the wrong sign is
`r pct(c4("stored", "wrong", test = "esvd", factor = "rank", level = "30"), 1)`
over the bank and
`r pct(c4("stored", "wrong", test = "esvd", factor = "shape", level = "gabitto_like"), 1)`
on the Gabitto-like cohorts (Table 26).

**Capped genes.** The package's false discoveries are
`r pct(c4("stored", "fdp", test = "esvd", status = "capped", factor = "rank", level = "30"), 1)`
of its calls on genes at the cap and
`r pct(c4("stored", "fdp", test = "esvd", status = "estimated", factor = "rank", level = "30"), 1)`
of its calls on the other genes (Table 25), and the Wald test of
`donor_wls@esvd_nofloor` has
`r pct(c4("donor_wls@esvd_nofloor", "fdp", status = "capped", factor = "rank", level = "30"), 1)`
and
`r pct(c4("donor_wls@esvd_nofloor", "fdp", status = "estimated", factor = "rank", level = "30"), 1)`.
The nuisance status therefore does not mark the package's false
discoveries on this bank, which agrees with the Green halves and not
with the second split of Gabitto. The test that the cap does hurt is the
Wald test of `raw@esvd_nofloor`, with
`r pct(c4("raw@esvd_nofloor", "fdp", status = "capped", factor = "rank", level = "30"), 1)`
false discoveries among its calls on capped genes, the genes whose
unfloored library is unstable at rank 30.

::: {.takeaway}
With effects of the size the Gabitto halves imply and a capped share
near theirs, the package's posterior-based test makes about three times
its nominal share of false discoveries, as it did on banks 2 and 3, and
the Wald test of `donor_wls@esvd_nofloor` stays within about a point of
5% with as many true DEGs called. The Wald test of `raw` is
anti-conservative with few donors. This is the evidence for taking the
p-value from the reported pair when the pair is `donor_wls`.
:::

# What two halves of a real cohort can and cannot measure

::: {.reuse}
The first block of `lfcse-bank-4` at rank 30. The two replicate cohorts
of an example stand in for the two halves of a real cohort, and every
statistic of the split-half reports is computed between them beside the
score against the truth.
:::

```{r bank4_replicates}
rep_method_vec <- c("stored", "null_rescaled", "raw", "raw@esvd_nofloor",
                    "raw_null", "donor_wls", "donor_wls@esvd_nofloor",
                    "donor_wls@total", "gap_trend", "state_adjusted",
                    "state_adjusted@esvd_nofloor", "deseq2")
rep_col_vec <- c(score_truth = "Score against the truth",
                 score_replicate = "Replicate score",
                 score_cross = "Score against the other replicate's DESeq2",
                 z_rms = "z_rms",
                 pearson_deg = "Correlation, true DEGs",
                 pearson_esvd = "Correlation, genes the package nominates",
                 esvd_sign_rep = "Sign kept, the package's calls")
rep_out_df <- data.frame(Method = paste0("`", rep_method_vec, "`"),
                         stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
for(col in names(rep_col_vec)){
  rep_out_df[[rep_col_vec[[col]]]] <- sapply(rep_method_vec, r4, col = col,
                                             factor = "rank", level = "30")
}
knitr::kable(rep_out_df, row.names = FALSE, digits = 2,
             caption = "Table 27. Between the two replicate cohorts of each example at rank 30 (first block): the score against the truth, and the statistics a split of a real cohort gives. Means over examples.")
```

```{r bank4_replicate_rank}
rep30_df <- repstrata4_df[repstrata4_df$factor == "rank" &
                            repstrata4_df$level == "30" &
                            repstrata4_df$method %in% focus_vec, ]
rank_cor <- function(col, bool_drop_state = FALSE){
  sub_df <- rep30_df
  if(bool_drop_state) sub_df <- sub_df[!grepl("^state_adjusted",
                                              sub_df$method), ]
  stats::cor(sub_df$score_truth, sub_df[[col]], method = "spearman")
}
# The package's calls: the bound from the sign agreement against the
# measured share of calls that are null or of the wrong sign.
stored30_df <- rep4_df[rep4_df$method == "stored" & rep4_df$rank == 30 &
                         rep4_df$tail == "gaussian" & rep4_df$capped == "low" &
                         is.finite(rep4_df$esvd_sign_rep), ]
bound_vec <- 2 * (1 - stored30_df$esvd_sign_rep)
```

**The replicate score ranks `state_adjusted` first on the bank as on the
two real cohorts, and the truth puts it behind every donor-level rule.**
At rank 30
its replicate score is `r fmt(r4("state_adjusted", "score_replicate", factor = "rank", level = "30"), 2)`
against `r fmt(r4("donor_wls@esvd_nofloor", "score_replicate", factor = "rank", level = "30"), 2)`
for `donor_wls@esvd_nofloor`, and its score against the truth is
`r fmt(r4("state_adjusted", "score_truth", factor = "rank", level = "30"), 2)`
against
`r fmt(r4("donor_wls@esvd_nofloor", "score_truth", factor = "rank", level = "30"), 2)`
(Table 27). Over the `r nrow(rep30_df)` methods of the table and their
variants, the rank correlation of the replicate score with the score
against the truth is `r fmt(rank_cor("score_replicate"), 2)`, and
`r fmt(rank_cor("score_replicate", bool_drop_state = TRUE), 2)` once the
`state_adjusted` variants are set aside. The score against the other
replicate's DESeq2 has a rank correlation of
`r fmt(rank_cor("score_cross"), 2)` with the truth's order, with the
`state_adjusted` variants included.

**The correlation over the true DEGs is the statistic that catches the
failure.** The two replicates of `state_adjusted` correlate at
`r fmt(r4("state_adjusted", "pearson_deg", factor = "rank", level = "30"), 2)`
over the true DEGs, where every rule that keeps the effect is above
`r fmt(min(rep30_df$pearson_deg[!grepl("^state_adjusted", rep30_df$method) & rep30_df$method != "raw@esvd_nofloor" & rep30_df$method != "raw@total"]), 2)`
(`raw@esvd_nofloor`
`r fmt(r4("raw@esvd_nofloor", "pearson_deg", factor = "rank", level = "30"), 2)`,
from the genes of section 12). On a real cohort the true DEGs are
unknown and the genes a test nominates take their place: over the genes
the package's test nominates the replicates of `state_adjusted`
correlate at
`r fmt(r4("state_adjusted", "pearson_esvd", factor = "rank", level = "30"), 2)`
against
`r fmt(r4("donor_wls@esvd_nofloor", "pearson_esvd", factor = "rank", level = "30"), 2)`
for `donor_wls@esvd_nofloor`, the same separation as on Gabitto (0.0
against 0.55 to 0.64) and Green (0.2 against 0.66).

**The gate on retained signal.** A scorer with replicate cohorts can
require that a rule's correlation over the true DEGs stay within a margin
of a reference rule's, and a scorer with a truth that `slope_deg` stay in
$[0.9, 1.1]$ beside `slope_weak`. At rank 30 `state_adjusted` fails both
(`slope_deg`
`r fmt(b4("state_adjusted", col = "slope_deg", factor = "rank", level = "30"), 2)`),
and every other rule of Table 19 passes the second.

**The bound from the sign agreement is loose.** Over the examples of the
bank the package's calls keep their sign in the other replicate
`r pct(mean(stored30_df$esvd_sign_rep))` of the time, which bounds their
null share at `r pct(mean(bound_vec))` on average, and the measured share
of calls that are null or of the wrong sign is
`r pct(mean(stored30_df$esvd_wrong), 1)`, less than half the bound. In a
single example the bound is an estimate from a few dozen calls, and the
measured share was within it in
`r pct(mean(stored30_df$esvd_wrong <= bound_vec + 1e-12))` of the
examples. The sign agreement of 66% to 88% on the real halves is
therefore compatible with a share of wrong calls near the bank's.

::: {.takeaway}
Of the statistics a split of a real cohort gives, the replicate score
cannot be trusted alone, as both split-half reports found, and the score
against an independent DESeq2 estimate together with the correlation over
nominated genes reproduces the truth's order on the bank. A bank with
replicate cohorts and a fitted rank of 30 would have stopped
`state_adjusted` at the gate.
:::

# Outlying donors and a high capped share

::: {.reuse}
The second block of `lfcse-bank-4` (`r num_examples4 - num_first4`
examples) at rank 30, beside the first block's examples with the same
number of donors and a third of them controls (`matched`).
:::

```{r bank4_block}
block_method_vec <- c("stored", "raw", "raw@esvd_nofloor", "raw@total",
                      "donor_wls", "donor_wls@esvd_nofloor",
                      "donor_wls@total", "deseq2")
block_table <- function(level_vec, label_vec, col, source = "strata",
                        digits = 3){
  wide4(block_method_vec,
        data.frame(factor = "block", level = level_vec, label = label_vec,
                   stringsAsFactors = FALSE),
        col = col, digits = digits, source = source)
}
outlier_level_vec <- c("matched_k30_n40", "outlier_k30_n40",
                       "matched_k30_n200", "outlier_k30_n200")
outlier_label_vec <- c("40 donors, Gaussian", "40 donors, outliers",
                       "200 donors, Gaussian", "200 donors, outliers")
knitr::kable(block_table(outlier_level_vec, outlier_label_vec, "score"),
             row.names = FALSE,
             caption = "Table 28. The score against the truth at rank 30 with Gaussian donor effects and with outlying donors.")
knitr::kable(block_table(outlier_level_vec, outlier_label_vec, "rmse",
                         digits = 3),
             row.names = FALSE,
             caption = "Table 29. The RMSE of the logFC (log2) in the same strata.")
knitr::kable(block_table(outlier_level_vec, outlier_label_vec, "pearson_all",
                         source = "replicate", digits = 2),
             row.names = FALSE,
             caption = "Table 30. The correlation of the logFC between the two replicate cohorts over all genes in the same strata, the statistic on which `donor_wls` fell behind `raw` on the Green halves.")
```

```{r bank4_block_pieces}
out4 <- function(method, col, level, source = "strata"){
  if(source == "strata") b4(method, col = col, factor = "block", level = level)
  else r4(method, col = col, factor = "block", level = level)
}
```

**Outlying donors at Green's rate cost `donor_wls` 0.11 to 0.14 nats and
cost `raw` and DESeq2 little.** With outlying donors the score of
`donor_wls@esvd_nofloor` goes from
`r fmt(out4("donor_wls@esvd_nofloor", "score", "matched_k30_n40"))` to
`r fmt(out4("donor_wls@esvd_nofloor", "score", "outlier_k30_n40"))` at 40
donors and from
`r fmt(out4("donor_wls@esvd_nofloor", "score", "matched_k30_n200"))` to
`r fmt(out4("donor_wls@esvd_nofloor", "score", "outlier_k30_n200"))` at
200; that of `raw` with the floored library goes from
`r fmt(out4("raw", "score", "matched_k30_n40"))` to
`r fmt(out4("raw", "score", "outlier_k30_n40"))` and from
`r fmt(out4("raw", "score", "matched_k30_n200"))` to
`r fmt(out4("raw", "score", "outlier_k30_n200"))`, and DESeq2's from
`r fmt(out4("deseq2", "score", "matched_k30_n40"))` to
`r fmt(out4("deseq2", "score", "outlier_k30_n40"))` and from
`r fmt(out4("deseq2", "score", "matched_k30_n200"))` to
`r fmt(out4("deseq2", "score", "outlier_k30_n200"))` (Table 28). The
order of the Green halves is reproduced: with outlying donors DESeq2 is
first, `raw` second and `donor_wls` third, where with Gaussian donors
`donor_wls` and DESeq2 are level and `raw` is behind. At 40 donors the
RMSE of `donor_wls@esvd_nofloor` rises from
`r fmt(out4("donor_wls@esvd_nofloor", "rmse", "matched_k30_n40"))` to
`r fmt(out4("donor_wls@esvd_nofloor", "rmse", "outlier_k30_n40"))` while
that of `raw` stays at
`r fmt(out4("raw", "rmse", "outlier_k30_n40"))` and DESeq2's at
`r fmt(out4("deseq2", "rmse", "outlier_k30_n40"))` (Table 29), and its
replicate correlation over all genes falls from
`r fmt(out4("donor_wls@esvd_nofloor", "pearson_all", "matched_k30_n40", "replicate"), 2)`
to
`r fmt(out4("donor_wls@esvd_nofloor", "pearson_all", "outlier_k30_n40", "replicate"), 2)`,
against
`r fmt(out4("raw", "pearson_all", "outlier_k30_n40", "replicate"), 2)` for
`raw` (Table 30). A donor at an eighth of the typical expression of a
gene moves the mean of logarithms that `donor_wls` regresses on and
barely moves the arithmetic mean of `raw` or the fitted mean of DESeq2's
negative binomial.

**What outlying donors do not break.** The interval of
`donor_wls@esvd_nofloor` still covers the truth
`r pct(out4("donor_wls@esvd_nofloor", "coverage_95", "outlier_k30_n40"), 1)`
and
`r pct(out4("donor_wls@esvd_nofloor", "coverage_95", "outlier_k30_n200"), 1)`
of the time at 40 and 200 donors, and the false discovery proportion of
its Wald test is
`r pct(c4("donor_wls@esvd_nofloor", "fdp", factor = "block", level = "outlier_k30_n40"), 1)`
and
`r pct(c4("donor_wls@esvd_nofloor", "fdp", factor = "block", level = "outlier_k30_n200"), 1)`:
the outliers enter its residual variance, so it loses precision and
power and stays valid. `raw@esvd_nofloor` is the worst of the table, for
the reason of section 12, which outlying donors aggravate.

```{r bank4_capped}
capped_level_vec <- c("matched_state_k30_n40", "capped_high_k30_n40",
                      "matched_state_k30_n200", "capped_high_k30_n200")
capped_label_vec <- c("40 donors, low", "40 donors, high",
                      "200 donors, low", "200 donors, high")
knitr::kable(block_table(capped_level_vec, capped_label_vec, "score"),
             row.names = FALSE,
             caption = "Table 31. The score against the truth at rank 30 with the lower and the higher capped share (`state = donor` in both).")
```

**A higher capped share does not reproduce the cost of the floor.** With
the Gamma rate on $(0.5, 50)$, 44 to 48% of the genes are capped or at
the boundary at rank 30 (Table 17), the share of the Green halves, and
the floored library costs `donor_wls`
`r fmt(out4("donor_wls", "score", "capped_high_k30_n200") - out4("donor_wls@esvd_nofloor", "score", "capped_high_k30_n200"))`
nats at 200 donors and
`r fmt(out4("donor_wls", "score", "capped_high_k30_n40") - out4("donor_wls@esvd_nofloor", "score", "capped_high_k30_n40"))`
at 40 (Table 31), against
`r fmt(out4("donor_wls", "score", "matched_state_k30_n200") - out4("donor_wls@esvd_nofloor", "score", "matched_state_k30_n200"))`
and
`r fmt(out4("donor_wls", "score", "matched_state_k30_n40") - out4("donor_wls@esvd_nofloor", "score", "matched_state_k30_n40"))`
at the lower share: nothing, in either case. The Green halves lost 0.25
and 0.40 nats to the floor, so the capped share is not what makes the
floor costly there, and this block does not identify what does. Bank 3,
whose genes reach 99% zeros, remains the bank that shows the cost of the
floor (section 7.3). The order of the rules is unchanged by the capped
share.

::: {.takeaway}
With outlying donors at the rate measured on Green, the bank reproduces
the order of the Green halves: `donor_wls` falls behind `raw` and
pseudobulk DESeq2 by 0.04 to 0.11 nats while keeping its coverage and
its false discovery proportion. With Gaussian donors it does not fall
behind `raw` at any number of donors, so the reversal on Green comes from the
outlying donors and not from the number of donors or of cells. Section
20 turns this into a check on the cohort.
:::

# Two real cohorts split in half

::: {.reuse}
No simulation. The Gabitto microglia (80 donors of about 500 nuclei, 27
controls) and the Green microglia (428 donors of about 190 nuclei, 152
controls) were each split twice into two donor-disjoint halves, each half
was fitted by `eSVD2::eSVD_helper()` at rank 30, and every rule was
compared between the halves
(`2026-11-15_gabitto/2026-11-15_gabitto-split-half_claude.Rmd`,
`2026-11-16_green/2026-11-16_green-split-half_claude.Rmd`). The replicate
score is the score of this document with the other half in place of the
truth, and `score_cross` scores a rule's pair against the other half's
DESeq2 estimate.
:::

```{r real_table}
real_method_vec <- c("stored", "null_rescaled", "raw", "raw@esvd_nofloor",
                     "raw@total", "donor_wls", "donor_wls@esvd_nofloor",
                     "donor_wls@total", "state_adjusted", "deseq2")
real_col_vec <- c(all_score = "score", score_cross = "score_cross",
                  all_z_rms = "z_rms", all_pearson = "corr_all",
                  esvd_pearson = "corr_nominated", esvd_sign_rep = "sign_rep")
real_out_df <- data.frame(Method = paste0("`", real_method_vec, "`"),
                          stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
for(col in names(real_col_vec)){
  for(cohort in c("gabitto", "green")){
    label <- paste0(real_col_vec[[col]], ", ",
                    c(gabitto = "Gabitto", green = "Green")[[cohort]])
    real_out_df[[label]] <- sapply(real_method_vec, function(method){
      rl(cohort, method, col)
    })
  }
}
knitr::kable(real_out_df, row.names = FALSE, digits = 2,
             caption = "Table 32. The two real cohorts, each number the mean of the cohort's two splits. `score` is the replicate score over all 5,256 genes and `score_cross` the score against the other half's DESeq2 (lower is better); `z_rms` is 1 when the SEs explain the disagreement between the halves; `corr_nominated` and `sign_rep` are over the genes the package's test nominates in at least one half.")
```

**What the two cohorts agree on.** `stored` has the worst score of the
rules that keep a signal on both (`r fmt(rl("gabitto", "stored", "all_score"), 2)`
and `r fmt(rl("green", "stored", "all_score"), 2)`), with an SE
`r fmt(1 / rl("gabitto", "stored", "all_z_rms"), 1)` and
`r fmt(1 / rl("green", "stored", "all_z_rms"), 1)` times too large.
`state_adjusted` has the lowest replicate score on both and halves that
correlate at `r fmt(rl("gabitto", "state_adjusted", "all_pearson"), 2)` and
`r fmt(rl("green", "state_adjusted", "all_pearson"), 2)`, the failure
sections 13 and 16 reproduce. Removing the posterior's floor from the
library helps `donor_wls` on both, by
`r fmt(rl("gabitto", "donor_wls", "all_score") - rl("gabitto", "donor_wls@esvd_nofloor", "all_score"), 2)`
nats on Gabitto and
`r fmt(rl("green", "donor_wls", "all_score") - rl("green", "donor_wls@esvd_nofloor", "all_score"), 2)`
on Green.

**Where they differ.** On Gabitto `donor_wls@esvd_nofloor` has the best
replicate score and the best `score_cross` of the rules that keep a
signal (`r rl_both("gabitto", "donor_wls@esvd_nofloor", "all_score")`
in the two splits against
`r rl_both("gabitto", "raw@esvd_nofloor", "all_score")` for
`raw@esvd_nofloor` and `r rl_both("gabitto", "deseq2", "all_score")` for
DESeq2). On Green `raw@esvd_nofloor` and DESeq2 are ahead of it
(`r rl_both("green", "raw@esvd_nofloor", "all_score")` and
`r rl_both("green", "deseq2", "all_score")` against
`r rl_both("green", "donor_wls@esvd_nofloor", "all_score")`). Over the
genes the package's test nominates, `donor_wls@esvd_nofloor` correlates
between the halves at least as well as `raw@esvd_nofloor` on both cohorts
(`r rl_both("gabitto", "donor_wls@esvd_nofloor", "esvd_pearson")` against
`r rl_both("gabitto", "raw@esvd_nofloor", "esvd_pearson")` on Gabitto,
`r rl_both("green", "donor_wls@esvd_nofloor", "esvd_pearson")` against
`r rl_both("green", "raw@esvd_nofloor", "esvd_pearson")` on Green).

**Why `donor_wls` trails on Green.** The Green report reran
`donor_wls@total` from the donor pseudobulk with one step changed at a
time. Over the genes with under 80% zeros its halves correlate at
`r dg_both("as the rule", "zeros_below_80")` as the rule stands, at
`r dg_both("as the rule, winsorized", "zeros_below_80")` when each gene's
log donor means are first pulled to within 3 MADs of the gene's median,
and at `r dg_both("no covariates, winsorized", "zeros_below_80")` when the
donor-level covariates are also left out, where `raw` on the same donor
sums has `r dg_both("raw (donor sums)", "zeros_below_80")`. On Gabitto
the same three versions give
`r dg_both("as the rule", "zeros_below_80", cohort = "gabitto")`,
`r dg_both("as the rule, winsorized", "zeros_below_80", cohort = "gabitto")`
and
`r dg_both("no covariates, winsorized", "zeros_below_80", cohort = "gabitto")`.
A few Green donors lie far from the others on the log scale for a gene,
and a mean of logarithms over 214 donors of about 190 nuclei gives them a
weight that an arithmetic mean does not.

**Calibration.** The `z_rms` of `donor_wls@esvd_nofloor` is
`r rl_both("gabitto", "donor_wls@esvd_nofloor", "all_z_rms")` on Gabitto
(an SE about 15% too large) and
`r rl_both("green", "donor_wls@esvd_nofloor", "all_z_rms")` on Green;
that of `raw@esvd_nofloor` is
`r rl_both("gabitto", "raw@esvd_nofloor", "all_z_rms")` and
`r rl_both("green", "raw@esvd_nofloor", "all_z_rms")`. A split cannot see
an SE that is too small for a reason both halves share, and section 14
shows that the interval of `raw` is too short with 13 controls; the
`z_rms` near 1 of `raw` on Gabitto is therefore not evidence that its
interval is honest there.

::: {.takeaway}
The two real cohorts confirm the simulated order at its ends (`stored`
and `state_adjusted` out; the unfloored library in) and divide on the
two candidates: `donor_wls@esvd_nofloor` on the cohort of few donors
with many nuclei, `raw@esvd_nofloor` on the cohort of many donors with
few, for a reason that is identified.
:::

# `raw` against `donor_wls`

::: {.reuse}
Everything above, restricted to the two candidates for the reported
pair, on one library at a time: the floored fitted library on banks 1 to
3 (the only one `raw` was run with there) and the unfloored fitted
library on the fourth bank and the real cohorts.
:::

```{r scorecard}
card_row <- function(source, weight, raw_val, wls_val, diff_text, win_text,
                     raw_cover, wls_cover, raw_fdp, wls_fdp, floor_val,
                     deseq2_val){
  data.frame(Evidence = source, Weight = weight,
             `raw` = raw_val, `donor_wls` = wls_val,
             `donor_wls minus raw (SE)` = diff_text,
             `donor_wls better` = win_text,
             `Coverage, raw` = raw_cover, `Coverage, donor_wls` = wls_cover,
             `FDP, raw` = raw_fdp, `FDP, donor_wls` = wls_fdp,
             `raw, floored library` = floor_val, `deseq2` = deseq2_val,
             check.names = FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
}
bank_card <- function(bank, label){
  p <- paired("donor_wls", "raw", bank = bank)
  card_row(label, "background", fmt(st("raw", bank = bank)),
           fmt(st("donor_wls", bank = bank)),
           paste0(fmt(p$diff), " (", fmt(p$se), ")"), pct(p$win),
           pct(st("raw", bank = bank, col = "coverage_95"), 1),
           pct(st("donor_wls", bank = bank, col = "coverage_95"), 1),
           pct(sg("raw", "own_fdp", bank = bank), 1),
           pct(sg("donor_wls", "own_fdp", bank = bank), 1),
           fmt(st("raw", bank = bank)), fmt(st("deseq2", bank = bank)))
}
bank4_card <- function(df, label, weight, factor, level){
  p <- paired4(pair_vec[2], pair_vec[1], df = df)
  card_row(label, weight, fmt(mean(df$score[df$method == pair_vec[1]])),
           fmt(mean(df$score[df$method == pair_vec[2]])),
           paste0(fmt(p$diff), " (", fmt(p$se), ")"), pct(p$win),
           pct(mean(df$coverage_95[df$method == pair_vec[1]]), 1),
           pct(mean(df$coverage_95[df$method == pair_vec[2]]), 1),
           pct(c4(pair_vec[1], "fdp", factor = factor, level = level), 1),
           pct(c4(pair_vec[2], "fdp", factor = factor, level = level), 1),
           fmt(mean(df$score[df$method == "raw"])),
           fmt(mean(df$score[df$method == "deseq2"])))
}
real_card <- function(cohort, label, weight){
  diff_vec <- real_df$all_score[real_df$cohort == cohort &
                                  real_df$method == pair_vec[2]] -
    real_df$all_score[real_df$cohort == cohort & real_df$method == pair_vec[1]]
  card_row(label, weight, fmt(rl(cohort, pair_vec[1], "all_score")),
           fmt(rl(cohort, pair_vec[2], "all_score")),
           paste0(fmt(diff_vec[1]), " and ", fmt(diff_vec[2])),
           paste0(sum(diff_vec < 0), " of 2 splits"), "", "", "", "",
           fmt(rl(cohort, "raw", "all_score")),
           fmt(rl(cohort, "deseq2", "all_score")))
}
rank30_df <- cohort4_df[cohort4_df$rank == 30, ]
gabitto_like_df <- rank30_df[rank30_df$shape == "gabitto_like", ]
outlier40_df <- rank30_df[rank30_df$tail == "outlier" &
                            rank30_df$donors == 40, ]
outlier200_df <- rank30_df[rank30_df$tail == "outlier" &
                             rank30_df$donors == 200, ]
card_df <- rbind(
  real_card("gabitto", "Gabitto halves (real; replicate score)", "high"),
  bank4_card(gabitto_like_df, "Bank 4, Gabitto-like, rank 30", "high",
             "shape", "gabitto_like"),
  real_card("green", "Green halves (real; replicate score)", "medium"),
  bank4_card(rank30_df[rank30_df$shape == "green_like", ],
             "Bank 4, Green-like, rank 30", "medium", "shape", "green_like"),
  bank4_card(outlier40_df, "Bank 4, 40 donors with outliers, rank 30",
             "medium", "block", "outlier_k30_n40"),
  bank4_card(outlier200_df, "Bank 4, 200 donors with outliers, rank 30",
             "medium", "block", "outlier_k30_n200"),
  bank4_card(first4_df[first4_df$rank == 5, ],
             "Bank 4, first block, rank 5", "background", "rank", "5"),
  bank_card("bank3", "Bank 3 (floored library)"),
  bank_card("bank2", "Bank 2 (floored library)"),
  bank_card("bank1", "Bank 1 (floored library)")
)
knitr::kable(card_df, row.names = FALSE,
             caption = "Table 33. The two candidates on every source of evidence, each on the unfloored fitted library where it was run with it (the real cohorts and bank 4) and on the floored one otherwise. Scores are against the truth on the banks and the replicate score on the real cohorts (nats per gene, lower is better); the difference is paired within cohorts, and `donor_wls better` is the share of cohorts in which it has the lower score. Coverage is of the 95% interval; FDP is the false discovery proportion of the rule's own Wald test at a nominal 5%, where the stratum has exact nulls. The last two columns are the scores of `raw` with the floored library and of pseudobulk DESeq2. The weight is the one the recommendation gives the row.")
```

```{r outlier_share}
# The share of log donor means more than 3 MADs below the gene's median,
# over the genes with under 80% zeros, on the two real cohorts.
outlying_df <- rbind(
  utils::read.csv(file.path("2026-11-16_green", "csv",
                            "outlying_donors_gabitto.csv")),
  utils::read.csv(file.path("2026-11-16_green", "csv",
                            "outlying_donors_green.csv"))
)
outlier_share_vec <- stats::setNames(outlying_df$share_below_3,
                                     outlying_df$cohort)
```

The rows of Table 33 are weighted as Kevin's note asks, towards the data
sets that resemble Gabitto. The Gabitto halves and the bank's cohorts of
40 or 80 donors with a third of them controls at the default rank carry
the decision. The Green halves, the bank's 200-donor cohorts and its
cohorts with outlying donors qualify it: the outlying donors are drawn
at the rate measured on Green
(`r pct(outlier_share_vec[["green"]], 1)` of the log donor means of the
well-expressed genes more than 3 MADs below the gene's median, against
`r pct(outlier_share_vec[["gabitto"]], 1)` on Gabitto), so those rows
describe Green's condition at either number of donors. Banks 1 to 3 and
rank 5 are background.

**On the rows of high weight `donor_wls` is ahead on every count.** It
has the lower replicate score in both splits of Gabitto (level in the
first, 0.06 nats ahead in the second), the lower score against the truth
in `r pct(paired4(pair_vec[2], pair_vec[1], df = gabitto_like_df)$win)`
of the Gabitto-like cohorts of the bank, a coverage of
`r pct(mean(gabitto_like_df$coverage_95[gabitto_like_df$method == pair_vec[2]]), 1)`
against
`r pct(mean(gabitto_like_df$coverage_95[gabitto_like_df$method == pair_vec[1]]), 1)`,
and a false discovery proportion of
`r pct(c4(pair_vec[2], "fdp", factor = "shape", level = "gabitto_like"), 1)`
against
`r pct(c4(pair_vec[1], "fdp", factor = "shape", level = "gabitto_like"), 1)`
for its own test. Against `raw` with the floored library, the form in
which `raw` is stable on the bank, `donor_wls@esvd_nofloor` leads by
`r fmt(-paired4(pair_vec[2], "raw", df = gabitto_like_df)$diff)` nats
(SE `r fmt(paired4(pair_vec[2], "raw", df = gabitto_like_df)$se)`) on
the Gabitto-like cohorts.

**On the rows of medium weight `raw` or DESeq2 is ahead wherever donors
are outlying.** `raw@esvd_nofloor` has the lower replicate score in both
splits of Green, by 0.03 and 0.07 nats. On the bank's cohorts with
outlying donors `donor_wls@esvd_nofloor` is behind `raw` with the floored
library by
`r fmt(paired4(pair_vec[2], "raw", df = outlier40_df)$diff)` nats at 40
donors and
`r fmt(paired4(pair_vec[2], "raw", df = outlier200_df)$diff)` at 200, and
behind DESeq2 by
`r fmt(paired4(pair_vec[2], "deseq2", df = outlier40_df)$diff)` and
`r fmt(paired4(pair_vec[2], "deseq2", df = outlier200_df)$diff)`
(section 17). It stays ahead of `raw@esvd_nofloor` on the bank in these
rows only because `raw` is unstable on the unfloored library at rank 30
there, which the real fits do not show (section 11). Without outlying
donors `donor_wls` is ahead of `raw` at 200 donors as at 40, and level
with DESeq2.

**On the background rows `donor_wls` is ahead throughout**, by
`r fmt(-paired("donor_wls", "raw", bank = "bank1")$diff)`,
`r fmt(-paired("donor_wls", "raw", bank = "bank2")$diff)` and
`r fmt(-paired("donor_wls", "raw", bank = "bank3")$diff)` nats on banks 1
to 3.

::: {.takeaway}
Weighted towards cohorts like Gabitto, the choice between the two
candidates is `donor_wls`: more accurate there, with an interval and a
test that hold their level at 13 controls. Its one weakness is
identified and measurable before any fit: donors that are outliers on
the log scale, 2.3% of donor-gene pairs on Green against 0.8% on
Gabitto, under which `raw` and pseudobulk DESeq2 are the more accurate
by 0.03 to 0.11 nats and `donor_wls` remains valid.
:::

# Recommendation

**Report the log2 fold change and its SE from `donor_wls`, reading the
fitted library before the posterior's floor (`donor_wls@esvd_nofloor`).**
This is the recommendation of the first version of this document and of
the Gabitto report, and it stands after the fourth bank and the two real
cohorts. Kevin's note of 2026-11-16 allows either `raw` or `donor_wls`
as the final method and asks that the choice be weighted towards data
sets like Gabitto. Each item below is marked as a consequence of the
evidence or as a choice.

- **`donor_wls` over `raw`** (a consequence, Table 33). On the Gabitto
  halves and on the bank's Gabitto-like cohorts it is the more accurate,
  its 95% interval covers at the nominal level with 13 controls where
  that of `raw` does not, and its Wald test keeps a false discovery
  proportion near 5% where that of `raw` exceeds it.
- **The unfloored fitted library** (a consequence, sections 7.3 and 18).
  The floor costs `donor_wls` 0.03 nats on Gabitto and 0.3 on Green.
  `donor_wls` reads the library through sums per donor and is stable on
  the unfloored one; `raw` is not, for the genes whose fitted depth
  coefficient is far from 1 (section 12). On a cohort whose covariates
  are all at the donor level the summed counts serve `donor_wls` as well
  (sections 7 and 12); the fitted library is kept because it is the
  better one when a covariate varies within donors (section 6).
- **The p-value from the same pair** (a consequence for the false
  discovery proportion, a choice for the package). The package's
  posterior-based test has three to four times its nominal false
  discovery proportion on banks 2, 3 and 4, and the Wald test of
  `donor_wls@esvd_nofloor` is near nominal on all four.
- **A check for outlying donors before the rule is trusted** (a
  consequence of the Green halves and of the bank's second block,
  sections 17 and 18; the threshold is a choice). On Green
  `donor_wls@esvd_nofloor` is 0.03 to 0.07 nats behind `raw@esvd_nofloor`
  and pseudobulk DESeq2, and on the bank's cohorts with outlying donors
  0.04 to 0.11 behind `raw` and DESeq2, because a mean of logarithms is
  moved by donors far below the others. The check needs no fit: the
  share of log donor means, over the genes with under 80% zeros, that
  lie more than 3 MADs below the gene's median. It is 0.8% on Gabitto,
  where `donor_wls` leads, and 2.3% on Green, where it trails; a share
  above about 1.5% is the proposed trigger for the replacement of step
  7.
- **Not `state_adjusted` at the default rank** (a consequence, sections
  13, 16 and 18). At rank 30 it removes about four fifths of every true
  effect in simulation and has no signal that replicates on either real
  cohort. At rank 5 it passes the gates and is the most accurate rule of
  the fourth bank, so the first version's statement that it is the rule
  for the effect at fixed cell state holds for a fit at a low rank only,
  and a real cohort fitted at a low rank is the experiment that would
  show whether it applies in practice.
- **Not `stored` as the reported SE** (a consequence, measured on four
  banks and two real cohorts), and not `gap_trend` (it fails `se_strong`
  on every bank).

::: {.recipe}
1. Fit eSVD-DE as now (`eSVD2::eSVD_helper()` or `eSVD()`), with every
   covariate in the design, cell-level ones included.
2. Rebuild the counts and the covariates of the fit and form the library
   $\ell_{cg} = \exp(z_g^\top C_c)$ over every covariate but the arm,
   **without** the floor at 0.1.
3. Run `donor_wls` (`autoresearch_lfcse/notes/RULE_nov11_claude.R`) on
   the counts, the design, the donor labels and that library. It returns
   the log2 fold change and its SE per gene: report this pair.
4. Report beside the pair the Wald z and its BH-adjusted p-value from the
   same pair. A gene called by the package's test and not by this one is
   a provisional call.
5. Before reading the pair, compute from the donor pseudobulk the share
   of log donor means, over the genes with under 80% zeros, that lie
   more than 3 MADs below the gene's median (0.8% on Gabitto, 2.3% on
   Green).
6. Flag genes with over 95% zero counts: their fold change is attenuated
   by about 13% (section 8).
7. Replacement: if the share of step 5 is above about 1.5%, or if on a
   split of the donors the halves of `donor_wls@esvd_nofloor` correlate
   worse over the genes with under 80% zeros than those of
   `raw@esvd_nofloor` (as on the Green halves), report the fold change
   and SE from `raw@esvd_nofloor`, after confirming that the fitted
   coefficient of the log summed count lies within 1 of 1 for the
   reported genes, and keep the Wald test of `donor_wls@esvd_nofloor`
   for the calls, which stays valid under outlying donors. A replicate
   score is never used alone to choose between rules (section 16).
:::

Whether step 4 replaces the package's posterior-based test, and whether
`compute_log_fold_change()` should compute `donor_wls@esvd_nofloor`, are
Kevin's decisions.

**What a next rule should try.** The evidence here does not propose a
rule, as Kevin asked for none, and it points at two. The first is
`donor_wls` with each gene's log donor means winsorized, which on the
Green halves replicates better than both candidates and on the Gabitto
halves changes nothing (section 18); the fourth bank's second block is
the place to score it. The second is `state_adjusted` on a second fit at
a low rank (section 13). The gates of section 16 are the ones a next
loop should add.

# What we glossed over

- **The banks are simulated from the eSVD model.** The fitted library's
  advantage at `confound = cell` assumes the covariates act
  log-linearly with one coefficient per gene, which is the model the fit
  assumes.
- **Rank 30 on 600 genes is a wider embedding, relative to the genes,
  than rank 30 on the 5,256 genes of the real cohorts.** The bank's
  rank-30 fits have depth coefficients far from 1 for a share of genes
  that the real fits do not have (section 11), so the instability of
  `raw@esvd_nofloor` at rank 30 is overstated by the bank; its coverage
  and its false discovery proportion with few donors do not depend on
  that.
- **The fourth bank has no cell-level covariate, no depth error and no
  state difference between the arms**, all of which bank 3 has. On it
  `donor_wls` and DESeq2 are level; the margin of `donor_wls` over DESeq2
  on banks 1 to 3 comes from settings the fourth bank leaves out.
- **The outlying donors of the second block are one mechanism**
  (expression lowered about eightfold for 15% of the genes of a tenth of
  the donors), with its rate and size measured on Green. On Green the
  outlying donors are the donors of low depth per nucleus (correlation
  -0.62 between a donor's share of outlying genes and its log depth),
  which the bank does not model; why they are outlying was not examined.
  A first version of the block with milder outliers (16 examples, ids
  `ex_0065` to `ex_0080`) did not move any rule and is no longer in the
  design; its files are still in the bank folder.
- **The threshold of 1.5% in step 7** lies between two cohorts and is
  not estimated from more than those two.
- **The higher capped share did not reproduce the cost of the floor**
  that Green shows (section 17); the bank's genes are not sparse enough
  for the floor to act.
- **Two splits of each real cohort**, which share all donors, are two
  looks at one data set. Differences under 0.03 nats or 0.05 in a
  correlation are within their variation.
- **A split cannot see a bias or an SE error that both halves share.**
  The banks are the evidence on those.
- **Each rule's own test uses a normal reference.** `donor_wls` has a
  moderated $t$ reference that would call slightly fewer genes with few
  donors.
- **DESeq2 is run one way**: pseudobulk by donor, default `DESeq()` and
  `results()`. No shrunken fold change, no cell-level model, no
  limma-voom or dreamlet.
- **The half count of `donor_wls`** attenuates the sparsest genes
  (section 8). Changing it would be a new rule and was not tried.
- **Winsorized log donor means are a diagnostic here**, computed with
  the summed-count library on two cohorts. They were not run on any bank
  and are not a proposed rule.
- **The first bank's cohort pairs** have different true effects by
  design, so only banks 3 and 4 supply replicates.
- **The intermediate commits of the loops** (38 and 19 experiments) were
  not rerun; only the reference rows and the kept rules were.
- **The floor exists for the posterior**, where a tiny library makes the
  Gamma-Poisson update unstable. This document shows only that the
  reporting rule should not inherit it.

# Files

Run from the repository root, in order within a folder.

| File | What it does |
|---|---|
| `2026-11-12_beyond-score/generator_claude.R`, `01_build-bank_claude.R` | the bank `lfcse-bank-3` (52 minutes on 5 cores, 427 MB) |
| `2026-11-12_beyond-score/02_apply-rules_claude.R <bank1\|bank2\|bank3>` | every rule, library variant and DESeq2 on every cohort of banks 1 to 3; per-gene results under `<LFCSE_BANK root>/lfcse-beyond-score/` |
| `2026-11-12_beyond-score/03_summarize_claude.R` | scores them and writes `2026-11-12_beyond-score/csv/` (sections 3 to 10) |
| `2026-11-12_beyond-score/csv/strata.csv`, `gene_bins.csv`, `sparsity_by_confound.csv`, `library.csv`, `significance.csv`, `replicates.csv.gz`, `replicate_genes.csv.gz`, `cohort_scores.csv.gz`, `bank3_cohorts.csv`, `bank_genes.csv`, `failures.csv` | the tables of sections 3 to 10, described in the first version of this document |
| `2026-11-16_beyond-score/generator_claude.R` | the bank `lfcse-bank-4`: design, population, cohort, one example (sourced after `autoresearch_lfcse2/harness/generator_claude.R`) |
| `2026-11-16_beyond-score/01_build-bank_claude.R` | builds the bank under `LFCSE_BANK` (`r num_examples4` examples, `r 4 * num_examples4` fits) |
| `2026-11-16_beyond-score/02_apply-rules_claude.R` | every rule, library variant and DESeq2 on every fitted cohort of bank 4; per-gene results under `<LFCSE_BANK root>/lfcse-beyond-score/bank4/` |
| `2026-11-16_beyond-score/03_summarize_claude.R` | scores them and writes `2026-11-16_beyond-score/csv/` (sections 11 to 17) |
| `2026-11-16_beyond-score/csv/bank4_strata.csv` | one row per method and stratum: score against the truth, diagnostics, head-to-head with DESeq2 |
| `2026-11-16_beyond-score/csv/bank4_calls.csv` | one row per method, test, nuisance status and stratum: calls, false discovery proportion, sign errors, true DEGs called |
| `2026-11-16_beyond-score/csv/bank4_replicates.csv`, `bank4_replicate_strata.csv` | one row per example, rank and method (and their means per stratum): the split-half statistics between the two replicate cohorts beside the score against the truth |
| `2026-11-16_beyond-score/csv/bank4_gene_bins.csv` | one row per method, rank and gene bin (sparsity, nuisance status, depth coefficient) |
| `2026-11-16_beyond-score/csv/bank4_cohort_scores.csv.gz`, `bank4_cohorts.csv`, `bank4_failures.csv` | one row per fitted cohort and method; realized values of the bank; non-finite returns |
| `2026-11-15_gabitto/`, `2026-11-16_green/` | the two split-half studies, each with its numbered scripts, `csv/` and report (section 18 reads `csv/summary.csv`, `csv/fits.csv` and `2026-11-16_green/csv/donor_wls_diagnosis_*.csv`) |
